pixel_description: Photorealistic oblique worm's-eye view from below-side of concrete footbridge deck with railing and pedestrian above. Top is stained concrete deck soffit. Below are two dark riveted longitudinal plate girders running fore-aft into depth on left and right with sky gap between. Spanning left-right between girders is a single light galvanized I cross-beam bolted at each end to vertical bracket assemblies with multiple bolts to girder webs. Hung centrally from cross-beam is a single rectangular square-tube cage support frame. Inside cage are four vertical steel coil springs at four corners plus one central vertical dark viscous cylinder with piston rod above it. Critical part mass: one single dark rust-brown rectangular block, wider than tall, centered below cage, its top face directly connected from above to bottom ends of the four springs and to bottom of central damper; clear air gap around sides for vertical motion. Below on left and right are two flat light perforated metal soffit screen panels hung horizontally by thin rods, with central rectangular gap exposing frame and mass. No text, numbers, arrows or callouts. No distinct small lock pin visible.

deviations.why: Pixels show 2 dark riveted longitudinal girders running fore-aft left and right with sky gap between. Undercount is merging/occlusion. Load support from both girders present, working principle unchanged.

Pixels show bolted bracket assemblies at both ends of cross-beam to girder webs/flanges. 8 small individual clamps not resolvable as separate metal clamp labels but mechanical girder-to-crossbeam connection present. Count/appearance difference does not change hung load path.
Pixels show 1 light galvanized I-beam spanning left-right between girders carrying central cage. Present and correctly oriented. Segmenter label miss, no real deviation.
Pixels show 1 central rectangular square-tube cage hung from cross-beam. Extra count is cross-beam double-counted as frame. Single frame holds springs/damper/mass correctly.

Pixels show 4 vertical coil springs at four corners of cage connecting frame top to mass top, all vertical. One tuned set realized as 4 coils still provides vertical stiffness tuned to 1.83 Hz and suspends mass vertically. Count increase does not change principle.
Pixels show 1 central vertical dark cylinder plus piston rod between frame top and mass top. Split into cylinder and rod gives 2 detections. Single vertical damping path present, orientation correct.

No distinct small pin resolved in pixels; pin is tiny and likely occluded inside frame or omitted in exposed view. Secondary inspection function only; primary mass-spring-damper energy dissipation intact.

Pixels show 2 perforated soffit leaves left and right with central gap exposing mass for illustration, hung below by thin rods. Two leaves are one screen shown open/retracted as cutaway. Size ratio measures single open leaf in perspective vs full closed screen. Aesthetic cover only, does not affect TMD dynamics.

s1_differences: All primary load-path parts present with correct connections, orientations and relative positions: 2 girders, 1 transverse cross-beam on end brackets, 1 central cage frame, 4 vertical coils representing 1 spring set, 1 central vertical damper, 1 block mass below, perforated screen shown as 2 open leaves. Differences are only 1 set rendered as 4 coils and 1 screen shown split open for visibility, plus unresolved tiny lock pin; none change vertical TMD working principle.
s2_feedback: Central cage shows four vertical springs and central vertical damper with clear air gap around block mass, cross-beam bolted to both girders, screens hung below without touching mass; load path girders->cross-beam->frame->springs/damper->mass continuous with free vertical travel, no interference, impossible assembly or unreachable part visible.
notes: Photorealistic render, no labels or diagram overlay. Screen shown open as illustrative cutaway to reveal TMD; lock pin too small to resolve. Segmenter over/undercounts verified against pixels as detection artefacts.
